# OpenCode Mobile

> OpenCode Mobile is a native Kotlin Android app (version 3.0.x) for running coding agents from your phone. It runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other agents in a Linux that the app installs on the phone through an agent helper, or connects to OpenCode 2 and other agents running on your computer.

The app needs Android 8 or newer; agents on the phone need a 64-bit phone. You ask for a change in a conversation, approve commands from a notification, a widget or the conversation, review the diff and use Git without leaving the app. Your conversations and code go only to the servers you choose, and it is MIT licensed. Version 3 installs over the 2.1 releases and keeps their data. The links below are the documents that are current for the native app; the Optional section is for people building or releasing it.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/README.md): What the app is, the agents it runs, how to install it and choose between this phone and a computer, compatibility, updating and signing.
- [Privacy policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/PRIVACY.md): Where your data goes, which connections the app accepts without HTTPS, and the optional reports and usage numbers that stay off unless you turn them on.
- [Release notes 3.0.2+10140](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/releases/v3.0.2+10140.md): The newest release: long conversations no longer run the app out of memory, a reply's steps sit where they happened, a provider you added can be edited and removed, and the faults 3.0.1 listed as known are fixed.
- [Release notes 3.0.1+10130](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/releases/v3.0.1+10130.md): Newer agents on the phone that update after asking, a floating conversation page, your own Stop respected, Japanese and Italian, and fixes found on real phones.
- [Release notes 3.0.0+10070](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/releases/v3.0.0+10070.md): The first public native release: what changed for you in the step list, New conversation, phone storage and projects, agents on this phone and their updates, and your own agents and providers.
- [Release notes 3.0.0+10030](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/releases/v3.0.0+10030.md): What changed for you in conversations, permissions, Home, agents on this phone, and computers and AI Team.
- [Release notes 3.0.0+10020](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/releases/v3.0.0+10020.md): The first native release, with the migration notes for people coming from 2.1.5, such as needing OpenCode 2 on the computer.
- [Run OpenCode 2 on a computer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/ubuntu-host.md): Install and start a loopback-only OpenCode 2 server, bring it within reach of the phone with USB, SSH or HTTPS, and pair with opencode2 pair.
- [Connect to Codex on a computer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/codex-connection.md): Start Codex app-server with a capability token, reach it with a tunnel or wss, add it in the app, and what the connection supports.
- [Connect to Claude Code through Paseo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/paseo-connection.md): Run the Paseo daemon beside your agent command-line tools without its relay, listen on a private network, and add it in the app.
- [Run an AI team on a computer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/ai-team-host.md): Set up a Gas City supervisor on a computer so the phone shows and steers several agents on your private network. The on-phone section is older.
- [Use the app with a server you already have](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/switching-clients.md): Open the conversations an OpenCode server already holds, what is shared with other clients, what stays on the phone, and how to connect over a network.
- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/CONTRIBUTING.md): Toolchain, the checks a change must pass, test naming, module boundaries, the two security rules, pull request contents and how reports are triaged.

## Optional

- [Native build rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/native/AGENTS.md): Toolchain versions, the module and testing rules for the Kotlin code, and a table of the Gradle tasks to run for each need.
- [Release procedure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/native/release.md): How a native release is built, gated, tagged and published as a draft, and how a broken release is fixed forward with a higher version code.
- [Release identity and signing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/native/release-identity.md): Which package and signing key each build uses, why a build must install over the last one, and which processor types ship.
- [Strings and translations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/native/tools/strings/README.md): The pipeline for adding English copy and keeping the other languages in step, with the drift check, glossaries and priorities.
- [Check ladder and push gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/native/tool/README.md): The scripts that run a module's tests while editing, before a push and at a checkpoint, and what their exit codes mean.
- [Behaviour catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/native/catalog/README.md): The list of behaviours the app must keep, which tests are named after, and the rules for adding to it.
- [Health and diagnostics telemetry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/telemetry/health-and-diagnostics.md): The consent choices, the fixed values that may be sent, and what is never sent, for the optional usage, crash and problem reports.
- [Moving from the Flutter app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eslamasabry/opencode-mobile-next/master/docs/native/migration/README.md): Every store the 2.1.5 app kept on a phone and how version 3 reads it, so updating in place keeps servers, settings and projects.
